collection.label: Corpus Hermeticum
collection.author_name: Hermes Trismegistus (attributed), 2nd-3rd century AD; Florence manuscript Laur. Plut. 71.33
collection.critical_edition: Parthey, Hermetis Trismegisti Poemander (1854): CH I via Greek Wikisource, CH XIII transcribed from the 1854 page images
collection.search_terms: corpus hermeticum hermes trismegistus poimandres poemandres pimander nous logos ascent become god rebirth regeneration palingenesia tat secret hymn ficino laurenziana mead
collection.description: The Hermetic Poimandres (CH I), the vision of the divine Mind and of the soul's ascent to become God, and the secret discourse on rebirth (CH XIII), shown section by section on the oldest manuscript of the Corpus Hermeticum, with Parthey's Greek and G. R. S. Mead's English.

texts.title: Corpus Hermeticum I: Poimandres
texts.source: Florence, Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Plut. 71.33 fol. 123r-125v (Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Teca digitale (IIIF)) + Parthey's Greek (1854, Wikisource) + G. R. S. Mead's English (1906)
texts.description: The first Hermetic treatise: the vision of Poimandres, the divine Mind, on the making of the world, the fall of the archetypal Man and the soul's ascent through the seven spheres to God, shown complete on the 14th-century Florence manuscript Laur. Plut. 71.33.

texts.title: Corpus Hermeticum XIII: the Secret Discourse on the Mountain, on Rebirth
texts.source: Florence, Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Plut. 71.33 fol. 141v-144r (Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Teca digitale (IIIF)) + Parthey's Greek (1854, transcribed from the page images) + G. R. S. Mead's English (1906)
texts.description: Hermes teaches his son Tat the way of rebirth: the twelve torments of matter are driven out by ten powers of God, Tat is born again in Mind and sings the secret hymn of rebirth. Complete, shown on the 14th-century Florence manuscript Laur. Plut. 71.33.
